items.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
items.content_text: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta’s Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. The discussions, which could end Amazon’s block on Muse, reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant’s advertising revenue. As reported by Fortune, Amazon is concerned that it could lose advertising revenue by allowing Muse on its site, since it depends on actual humans seeing ads across its online mar

items.title: Trump to Lead TSMC Groundbreaking in Arizona After Nvidia Gambit
items.content_text: US President Trump is scheduled to lead the groundbreaking ceremony for the TSMC Arizona fab on December 4. This event serves to highlight the political commitment to onshoring advanced chip manufacturing, with market participants closely watching for policy signals regarding incentives, tariffs, and production timelines.

items.title: Behind Binance Hack, a Reckoning Over Who Controls Crypto
items.content_text: During the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.5 billion in USDT and $1.1 billion in USDC within 30 minutes, respectively. This action marks a significant shift as the two issuers utilized centralized control over their smart contracts to execute immediate asset blocks upon requests from government authorities and the affected exchange.

items.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
items.content_text: Google DeepMind VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu announced that AI agents now manage partial compute for Gemini experiments, transitioning from project-specific teams to a unified general-purpose algorithm architecture. This shift aims to accelerate iteration cycles while preventing recursive self-improvement to maintain human-verifiable control over model reasoning.

items.title: OpenAI publishes a preprint that claims to prove that the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4, addressing a major open problem in mathematics (alphaXiv)
items.content_text: OpenAI published a preprint proving that the square matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4 over any field. Utilizing formal arithmetic circuits and proof by contradiction, the research bridges matrix multiplication efficiency with lower bounds on network compression costs, filling a critical gap in asymptotic rank and unrestricted circuit complexity.

items.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
items.content_text: AI models keep getting better, but putting them to work mostly creates friction, a new Anthropic report finds. Review bottlenecks, employee pushback, security risks, and outdated custom tools are dragging down many enterprise projects. Anthropic's researchers conducted 66 in-person interviews at 58 US companies for the qualitative study, from AI startups to established firms in law, construction, finance, medicine, and manufacturing. items.title: PhonePe Revives IPO Plans, Eyes March 2027 Listing At Up To $15 Bn Valuation
items.content_text: Walmart-backed fintech major PhonePe has revived its IPO plans and restarted discussions with investment bankers, targeting a March 2027 listing at a valuation of $12 Bn to $15 Bn, sources told Inc42. The Bengaluru-based company plans to file updated IPO papers by December-end for an offer for sale of up to ₹12,000 Cr ($1.3 Bn). items.title: PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values
items.content_text: Startup PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an updated version of its aggressively compressed language model. It's based on Qwen3.8-27B and takes up just 5.9 GB of memory, same as its predecessor. That's possible because of ternary quantization, where each weight can only be one of three values (−1, 0, or +1) instead of the usual 16-bit storage. Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. items.title: Asia Data Centers Sound Out US Clients to Replace China Demand
items.content_text: The US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued an interim final rule, effective around November 16, 2026, targeting remote access to high-end AI compute by Chinese entities at non-US data centers. Facilities providing significant compute, exceeding 12 million aggregate TPP, are required to implement enhanced due diligence and obtain licenses, facing potential trade restrictions for non-compliance.

items.title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
items.content_text: Researchers from MIT, ETH Zurich, and Imperial College London have developed a method to train AI climate emulators using synthetic data characterized by extreme environmental fluctuations, such as sudden CO2 spikes. This approach allows models to achieve high precision and robustness with only a single simulation run, significantly reducing computational demand.

items.title: Exclusive: Meta and Amazon discuss ending Muse shopping bot blockade, as ads, search emerge as key issues
items.content_text: Meta Platforms and Amazon are negotiating the potential integration of Meta's Muse AI agent into Amazon's e-commerce platform, seeking to reverse a block imposed two months ago. The core tensions involve potential cannibalization of Amazon's advertising revenue and the risks of disintermediation between brands and their end consumers.

items.title: Australia passes the Digital Duty of Care Act, an online safety law that exposes Big Tech to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable harms (Rod McGuirk/Associated Press)
items.content_text: The Australian Parliament has passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, legally mandating that Big Tech companies take proactive measures to prevent foreseeable online harms. Backed by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, the legislation allows for fines of up to 5% of global revenue, though it faces intense criticism over potential political censorship and free speech concerns.

items.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
items.content_text: AI-powered automation is triggering a surge in public records requests across the U.S., forcing local agencies to handle significantly increased volume and scope. This influx has strained the limited resources of town and state offices, leading some jurisdictions to consider legislative changes to limit transparency requirements, potentially hindering open government.

items.title: Chinese EDA software provider Phlexing says it has been collaborating with Huawei since 2019 to develop a suite of EDA tools based on Huawei's Tau Scaling Law (Nikkei Asia)
items.content_text: Huawei and Phlexing Technology have collaborated since 2019 to integrate chip architecture, workflows, and EDA tools. Leveraging Huawei’s 'Tau Scaling Law,' the project aims to resolve automation challenges in advanced chip design, circumventing US-imposed Entity List restrictions.

items.title: Brussels presses porn sites to introduce tougher age checks
items.content_text: The European Commission is pressuring adult platforms, including Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX, and XVideos, to implement more robust age verification. This effort aligns with the development of a bloc-wide age verification application aimed at enhancing minor protection in the digital space.

items.title: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)
items.content_text: Huawei Technologies announced that HarmonyOS has surpassed 100 million installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, supported by over 460,000 apps and 12 million registered developers. Richard Yu Chengdong, Chairman of the Consumer Business Group, stated that the ecosystem has crossed a critical scale threshold, signaling the system's transition to a mature, self-reliant software platform independent of Google’s mobile services.

items.title: Sources: Samsung and SK Hynix agree to adopt parts of YMTC's "Xtacking" tech for 3D NAND flash via cross-licensing deals, signaling YMTC's rapid tech progress (Nikkei Asia)
items.content_text: Global memory leaders Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have integrated Yangtze Memory Technologies Co.'s (YMTC) Xtacking architecture via cross-licensing deals, utilizing independent CMOS and cell wafer bonding to optimize 3D NAND performance. This adoption confirms YMTC’s rapid technical maturation and patent portfolio depth, marking a significant milestone in China's semiconductor industrial self-sufficiency.

items.title: Amazon Targets UK Car Buyers Being Reeled In by Chinese Brands
items.content_text: Amazon.com Inc. has announced plans to launch online car retail services in the UK by early 2027. This expansion builds upon its established US footprint, where it currently facilitates new and used car sales across 35 brands in over 150 cities, signaling a push to capture automotive market share through e-commerce channels.

items.title: ‘Tech bros strike back’ as Donald Trump rescues Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated after Silicon Valley investors, including Marc Andreessen, lobbied Vice President JD Vance and President Trump. Despite national security concerns raised by Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding alleged spy ties, Trump prioritized the AI-led economic boom and tech market stability, supported by Attorney General Todd Blanche’s confirmation of no evidence of wrongdoing.

items.title: NJ-based AidenAI, which helps enterprises integrate AI into apps, data infrastructure, and business workflows, raised a $32M Series A led by A91 Partners (Anne Florentyna/Inc42)
items.content_text: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities.
